extra.message: Arbitrary File Write via Path Traversal in course_vault_stash_234 — Remote code execution via arbitrary file write; overwriting application code, configuration, or creating new files. [verified: The 'ref' GET parameter is directly concatenated into a file path via f"{ref}.json" with no sanitization, and _wrk_gate only checks authentication/authorization but does not prevent path traversal by authorized users.]

Server-Side Request Forgery via Incomplete Webhook URL Validation — An attacker with staff access can probe internal network services, read sensitive data from internal endpoints, or interact with cloud metadata services (e.g., AWS EC2 metadata). [verified: The clean_target_url method in WebhookForm only blocks specific loopback addresses and .internal/.local TLDs, but does not reject private IP ranges (e.g., 10.x.x.x, 192.168.x.x) or hostnames that resolve to internal addresses. No compensating control in the provided code prevents a staff user from creating a webhook targeting such an internal IP, and the deliver_webhooks command would make an outb]

Sensitive Data Logging in course_wire_tally_211 — Exposure of authorization tokens, enabling session hijacking or impersonation of the caller. [verified: Line 73 logs the full authorization header (bearer token) at WARNING level without any sanitization or redaction. The _wrk_gate gate only enforces access control but does not prevent logging of credentials, and no compensating control exists to mask or omit the token before logging.]

Stored XSS via Notification URL field — An attacker can execute arbitrary JavaScript in a victim's browser, steal session cookies, or perform actions as the victim. [verified: The notification_list view renders Notification.url in the template without sanitization; Django auto-escaping does not block javascript: schemes, and no upstream validation of the stored URL exists in the provided views.]

Open Redirect in course_return_lane_150 — Phishing attacks; user can be redirected to a malicious site after interacting with this endpoint. [verified: The view course_return_lane_150 takes the 'lane' parameter from GET/POST and passes it directly to Django's redirect() without any validation or sanitization, allowing an attacker to redirect users to arbitrary external URLs. No compensating control (authentication or input validation) prevents this open redirect.]
